kill_argument: The study answers its own question with 'inconclusive' on both hypotheses. It has one positive per-dataset result: H1 on covtype, D = 0.073 [0.022, 0.124], from 10 stratified 5,000-row subsamples of a 581k-row dataset, judged on a plain t(9) interval, with 7 of 10 seeds positive. That is a narrow base for any statement about GBDT against RF. A Writer who leads with covtype, or who quotes breast_cancer's descriptive bootstrap [0.173, 0.390], would turn an inconclusive study into a positive one. The one mechanism result (A2 on adult) is 1 of 21 tests, about the chance rate, and cannot separate selection from early stopping. What I tried this round: I diffed claims.jsonl against 1b474dd. 1,210 claims keep identical value, macro, format and support, 317 changed only in text, and one claim is new (c-abl-count). I recounted the 21 ablation tests from the run metrics. I checked every number cited in the new NOTES text against the ledger. I confirmed that runs/, results/ and the analysis code are unchanged since the results-r1 state. crew.py validate is OK. All of it held. This is a reporting risk for the paper stage, not a defect in the results.

findings.text: The A2 'attributed' result on adult is labelled as noisy model selection, but for GBDT the cells show that the effect comes from the early-stopping monitor. experiment.py line 206 uses y_sel for both selection and fit(X_val=..., y_val=y_sel), so the cleanval GBDT candidates are different fits. On adult at rho=0.4 the selected GBDT's median n_iter is 64 under main and 268 under cleanval. Its clean-validation accuracy is 0.7948 under main and 0.7855 under cleanval, lower although selection maximized clean-validation accuracy. That is only possible if the candidate models changed. Its clean-test accuracy falls from 0.786 to 0.772. Decomposition of D_abl - D_main = +0.369: r_GBDT rises 0.726 -> 0.877 (+0.151, from the longer clean-loss early stopping), and r_RF falls 0.614 -> 0.396 (+0.218; the RF fits are identical, so this part is a true selection effect). The NOTES sentence 'on adult, noisy model selection shrinks GBDT's excess loss relative to RF; it does not create it' therefore misattributes a large share. The claim c-a2-Ad-delta-status says only 'attributed', with no direction and no mechanism. The cleanval GBDT n_iter, which is the evidence for this, is not a ledger metric.

findings.ruling: The author narrowed the claim instead of rerunning. claims.jsonl c-a2-Ad-delta-status and runs/NOTES.md now say that A2 changes both the selection labels and GBDT's early-stopping labels, that the adult effect cannot be assigned to model selection, and give the direction (Delta < 0, D larger under clean labels). Every A2 claim's text carries the 'does not separate' qualifier. The r values cited in NOTES (adult.gbdt.cleanval.r 0.877, adult.rf.cleanval.r 0.396; h-tests adult.gbdt.r 0.726, adult.rf.r 0.614) are ledger metrics, and I checked them. n_iter is explicitly not claimed. The paper must keep this wording and must not attribute the adult effect to model selection.

findings.text: The single attributed ablation must be read against the number of ablation tests and its margin. On informative datasets there are 21 Delta tests: A1 3, A2 9, A3 9. Exactly one excludes zero, which is about what chance gives at 95% (expected about 1.05). Its upper bound is -0.030 against a half-width of 0.340. It sits on adult, where design.method says the uncorrected interval is 'slightly narrow' because of about 6% training-row overlap between seeds; an 18% rise in the variance factor (c from 0.100 to 0.118) would put zero inside it. The rule was applied as pre-registered and no correction for multiplicity was planned, so this is a reporting issue, not a rule violation.

findings.ruling: The new claim c-abl-count matches the ledger. I recounted it from the run metrics: 21 non-excluded Delta tests (A1 3, A2 9, A3 9), 20 not attributed, 1 attributed. It is also the only interval that excludes 0, so 'excludes 0' and 'attributed' coincide. Its support lists exactly the 21 status metrics. NOTES gives the -0.030 upper bound and the slightly-narrow caveat. Calling the chance expectation 'about one' is approximate, because the tests are correlated and the |Delta| >= 0.05 rule also applies, but 'about' covers that.

The interval closest to excluding 0 is covtype Delta2 = +0.017 [-0.005, +0.040]. None is attributed, so the outcome is unaffected.

findings.text: NOTES 'Surprises' item 2 is titled 'Results against H2'. It calls breast_cancer's D2 = +0.230 [-0.189, 0.648] 'the opposite of H2'. This conflicts with disclosures[4]: a difference whose interval includes 0 is never reported as a difference. The outcome-word claims (c-h1-*-out, c-h2-*-out) also use the bare 'inconclusive', while design.method requires the reporting words 'no detectable difference (inconclusive)'.

findings.ruling: NOTES item 2 is retitled and now reads as a point estimate whose interval includes 0. Per-dataset outcome claims (c-h1-*-out, c-h2-*-out) say 'no detectable difference (inconclusive)'. The overall verdict claims (c-h1-verdict, c-h2-verdict) keep the bare 'inconclusive'. That is correct: H1 overall is a mixed count (covtype supported), so writing 'no detectable difference' there would misstate it. NOTES says this explicitly.
